subject.title: Incomplete turn with tool call and payloads=0 is replayUnsafe and may poison session state

question: For a stopReason=stop turn with tool calls but zero payloads, should the embedded runner retry or fail over when the current attempt has no side effects, or always quarantine the turn as replay-unsafe?
rationale: Both paths are plausible and compatibility-sensitive: retry/failover improves recovery for provider flakes, while quarantine is safer when the runtime cannot prove that tool-call side effects are absent.

options.title: Retry clean current attempts
options.body: Use current-attempt side-effect metadata to consume empty retry/fallback budgets only when the malformed turn cannot repeat actions, and quarantine unsafe attempts.

options.title: Always quarantine tool-call empty turns
options.body: Persist a structured terminal quarantine for every tools>0/payloads=0 stop turn and require explicit recovery instead of automatic retry.

options.title: Limit fix to cron fallback
options.body: Rely on cron fallback work for scheduled jobs and leave interactive embedded turns on the existing incomplete-turn error path.

recommendation.title: Retry clean current attempts
recommendation.body: Use current-attempt side-effect metadata to consume empty retry/fallback budgets only when the malformed turn cannot repeat actions, and quarantine unsafe attempts.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest maintainer-side review history on the adjacent incomplete-turn recovery and replay-safety policy decisions.
